FLCI weights on the pre-treatment coefficients

Source: R/weights.R
flci_weights.Rd

Tabulate the linear weights of fixed-length confidence intervals (FLCIs): the weights v on the pre-treatment coefficients or the weights gamma on the pure pre-treatment second differences, for every target and bound of an FLCI result. plot(x, type = "weights") draws them.

Usage

flci_weights(
  x,
  weights = c("coefficients", "gamma"),
  by = c("element", "cohort")
)

Arguments

x

A cohort_sensitivity object computed with method = "FLCI".

weights

"coefficients" (default) for the weights v on the pre-treatment coefficients, or "gamma" for the weights on the pure pre-treatment second differences.

by

"element" (default) for one row per coefficient or second difference, or "cohort" for sums over each cohort's rows (cohort inference only).

Value

A data frame. With by = "element": one row per target, bound and element, with columns target and label (the target's id and label), M, cohort (NA under aggregate inference), relative_period (the coefficient's period, or the last period of the second difference), element (the coefficient name, or d2_g<cohort>_s<period> for a second difference), weight, estimate (the coefficient estimate, or the estimated second difference), contribution (weight times estimate), and tie.break (TRUE when the FLCI chose its weights by the minimum-norm rule described below). With by = "cohort": one row per target, bound and cohort, with elements (the number of rows summed), weight (their sum), l1 (the sum of absolute weights), share (the cohort's part of the total l1), contribution (the sum of contributions), and tie.break. Rows follow the targets, then the sorted bounds, then cohorts and periods in increasing order. Attributes: weights, by, framework, full.path; centers, one row per target and bound with the conventional estimate, the post-only center post.only.center, and the FLCI center; and missing, the targets and bounds whose FLCI failed and that therefore have no weights, with their status.

Details

The FLCI is a linear estimator: its weights on the post-treatment coefficients are the target weights, and its weights on the pre-treatment coefficients are v. Under the post-only SD restriction, v is fixed at the post-only weights, which subtract each cohort's linear extrapolation from its last two pre-treatment periods (with CS-NYT, they also undo the base-period correction of the adjustment cohorts); the resulting estimate is the post-only center. Under the full-path restriction, v equals the post-only weights plus t(D) %*% gamma, where the rows of D form the pure pre-treatment second differences zhat = D %*% betahat, and the FLCI center is the post-only center plus sum(gamma * zhat). Hence the contributions of the gamma rows add up to the FLCI center minus the post-only center, and those of the v rows to the FLCI center minus the conventional estimate. The post-only FLCI has gamma = 0.

Each cohort's pre-treatment coefficients satisfy one normalization (CS: the coefficient at period 0 is zero; imputation: they sum to zero), so weights that differ along it give the same estimate. flci_weights() reports v in the form above, the paper's; results[[k]]$weights$coefficients stores its projection orthogonal to the normalization. The cohort sums of the contributions are the same for both.

Under aggregate inference the rows are the aggregated coefficients and their second differences. With balanced = TRUE and cohort.paths = "window", the gamma rows are the second differences inside the balanced window. When several weight vectors give the same FLCI length, as can happen at M = 0, the FLCI uses the one with the smallest Euclidean norm of gamma; tie.break marks these rows.

See also

cohort_sensitivity, plot_cohort

Examples

data(minimum_wage)
# \donttest{
fit <- cohort_fit(Y ~ D, minimum_wage, index = c("id", "year"))
full <- cohort_sensitivity(fit, M = c(0, 0.005, 0.01), method = "FLCI",
                           seed = 1)
post <- cohort_sensitivity(fit, M = c(0, 0.005, 0.01), method = "FLCI",
                           full.path = FALSE, seed = 1)
head(flci_weights(full))
#>   target                    label M cohort relative_period          element
#> 1    att Average treatment effect 0      4              -2 delta_pre_g4_s-2
#> 2    att Average treatment effect 0      4              -1 delta_pre_g4_s-1
#> 3    att Average treatment effect 0      4               0  delta_pre_g4_s0
#> 4    att Average treatment effect 0      6              -4 delta_pre_g6_s-4
#> 5    att Average treatment effect 0      6              -3 delta_pre_g6_s-3
#> 6    att Average treatment effect 0      6              -2 delta_pre_g6_s-2
#>        weight     estimate  contribution tie.break
#> 1  0.31191871 -0.019067503 -5.947511e-03     FALSE
#> 2  0.07546328  0.004858126  3.666101e-04     FALSE
#> 3 -0.66710227  0.014209377 -9.479107e-03     FALSE
#> 4  0.11920927 -0.012605613 -1.502706e-03     FALSE
#> 5  0.01119890 -0.038937371 -4.360558e-04     FALSE
#> 6  0.02502148  0.003400663  8.508961e-05     FALSE
flci_weights(full, weights = "gamma", by = "cohort")
#>   target                    label     M cohort elements    weight        l1
#> 1    att Average treatment effect 0.000      4        1 0.3119187 0.3119187
#> 2    att Average treatment effect 0.000      6        3 0.7738738 0.7738738

#> 6    att Average treatment effect 0.005      7        4 0.0000000 0.0000000

#> 9    att Average treatment effect 0.010      7        4 0.0000000 0.0000000
